page: Amazon Web Services a1.xlarge is a first-generation ARM-based instance powered by four dedicated AWS Graviton Cortex-A72 physical cores operating at 2.3 GHz on the Nitro hypervisor. It includes 8.0 GB of memory, yielding a ratio of 2.0 GB per core, with 32 KB of L1d cache and 2 MB of L2 cache. The instance contains no bundled local NVMe storage and no GPU accelerators. Baseline network performance is rated at 1 Gbps with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The arm64 CPU architecture supports hardware AES encryption, though it lacks x86-specific instruction sets such as AVX vector extensions or Advanced Matrix Extensions.

Benchmark evaluations reveal modest performance metrics across computational and memory tasks. Single-core stress-ng tests place the processor in the middle 50% percentile with a score of 1488.48, while multi-core stress-ng throughput falls into the bottom 25% at 5919.11. Memory bandwidth testing shows 140.34 GB/sec for cached small-block operations, dropping to 12.56 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 6.77 GB/sec for writes. Synthetic benchmarks indicate a Geekbench single-core score of 408.0 and multi-core score of 1245.0, alongside a PassMark CPU rating of 1618.39, reflecting lower overall execution density compared to newer processor architectures.

The a1.xlarge instance provides dedicated physical core allocation, offering predictable resource availability for workloads that do not require high single-thread clock speeds or x86 acceleration. Static web serving achieves 1.36 GB/sec throughput, while Redis handles up to 2.13 million SET operations per second. Small LLM inference tests using a 135M model deliver 76.29 prompt tokens per second and 6.69 text generation tokens per second. The hardware profile is suitable for lightweight microservices, arm64 application compiling, basic CI/CD build nodes, and low-traffic web applications.
